issues.description: The problem statement's UML shows acceptSupplyDelivery(String,int,int): void as a normal public method (no indication of static), but elsewhere in the problem text it explicitly requires acceptSupplyDelivery to be static (shared across all saloons). The reference solution implements acceptSupplyDelivery as a static method. This inconsistency between the UML and the textual requirement can confuse students about whether to implement acceptSupplyDelivery as an instance or static method and how to call it.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either update the UML in problem_statement.md to indicate acceptSupplyDelivery is static (e.g., by mentioning 'static' in the UML or text near the method) or remove the textual requirement that it be static. Also update example usage (Main) to call the method in the intended way (static call via SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery(...) if static), so students have an unambiguous model to follow.
